habitat: Parties of three to eight in woodland or well-wooded suburbia. They fly from tree to tree, settle low, and work upwards.
summary: A common resident. Larger than Common Scimitarbill, deep iridescent blue, with a green-and-blue head, a curved red bill, red feet and a long tail. The immature has a black bill, less decurved than a Common Scimitarbill’s. The call is a high-pitched cackle started by one bird and taken up by the party. The Kemp paper name Redbilled Woodhoopoe and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Common Scimitarbill is smaller, with a black, more decurved bill and a shorter tail.
